text: Validate the actual native openvela factory coffee UI by rendering with the real local LVGL on the host, no hardware claims. Write ONLY under /mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/ui-render-check. Do not modify maintained sources, no full firmware builds/hardware/other workers. Root integrated candidate at openvela-dev/frameworks/runtimes/services/xmsdemo/factory (will continue root integration); stable copies UI in backups/factory-demo-port/ui-port/candidate/.../factory, asset provider in assets-port/candidate. Reuse actual LVGL build/config/harness knowledge under assets-port/tools/run_host_validation.py and validation/host. Need actual 800x480 RGB565 renders of dashboard and all 12 original coffee screens including animations/transitions; original pinned Espressif UI under upstream/.../factory_demo/ui. Compile C pure CoffeeWindow and copied generated UI, fonts, asset provider, FactoryDashboard.cpp with native headers if possible (dashboard C++ mainly pure LVGL/interface). Use real LVGL no screen stubs, correct widgets/fonts config and original PNG assets. Can test screen transitions/lifecycle create/destroy while using static host display buffer. Generate PNG/PPM images + contact sheet and receipt linking exact source hashes; compare obvious layout/clipping/missingasset failures. No need exhaustive test invention: prioritize visual verification and lifecycle risks before board, no fake performance claims. Read contracts/integration-review for actual root ownership rules. Host root panel must child of actual LVGL screen like WM; CoffeeWindow should not replace default screen/theme. If genuine code defects found, private patch only. Do not block worker on board. Deliver result.md plus images and exact commands promptly. Root handles native Activity lifecycle separately; don't duplicate that work.

I’ll read the integration rules and existing host harness, then render the native dashboard and coffee UI with local LVGL. I’ll keep all files under `ui-render-check` and limit the findings to host rendering and UI lifecycle behavior.

The ownership rules match your requirement: coffee panels must stay under a window root, with the shared active screen and theme unchanged. The existing asset harness provides the RGB565, PNG, cache, and filesystem settings; I’ll use those with the full software renderer and compile the dashboard against its native header.

I found a lifecycle issue to check: the bridge cancels water-wave and coffee-arrow animations when their panel is hidden, but each generated panel keeps an “already started” flag until destruction. I’ll verify whether those animations restart on return, alongside the 12 screen renders.

The dashboard, CoffeeWindow, generated UI, and fonts are frozen with source hashes; they match the stable UI candidate. The host build is running. I also prepared an isolated renderer for the pinned Espressif UI so the native frames can be compared against the original on the same LVGL.

The host build uses the local LVGL revision, which reports version 9.1.0. It has PNG decoding, RGB565 software drawing, the dashboard’s Montserrat fonts, and all ten generated coffee fonts enabled. The harness will capture entry-animation frames, exercise 25 registered click transitions, and check destruction with navigation timers and looping animations active.

Compilation found one additional font dependency: a generated slider component requires Montserrat 46. I’ve enabled it in the host config and kept the UI sources unchanged. The render comparison will use the original PNGs, and the dashboard will show explicit host-unavailable status text with a black camera canvas.

The first RGB565 render is complete. The dashboard’s main cards, labels, and controls are readable at 800×480. The lifecycle run is also progressing: repeated coffee destruction leaves the sibling window’s animation running. I’m now collecting the coffee frames and checking the animation-reentry result.

Both reentry defects are confirmed: the water wave and coffee arrows move on first entry, then stay frozen after returning to the panel. All 25 click transitions and the automatic Brewing → Done → Home and Ready → Home transitions passed. I’ve prepared a private patch to reset the two animation guards on unload and will verify it without changing the original snapshot.

All 12 coffee screens match the pinned original UI pixel-for-pixel at 100, 300, and 900 ms: 36 matching RGB565 captures. I also checked the contact sheet and brewing sequence; I found no new layout, clipping, or missing-image failures. The confirmed native defect is the two looping animations failing to restart on panel reentry.

The private patch restores both looping animations on reentry and passes the same transition and 24-cycle destruction checks. The address/undefined-behavior sanitizer run is nearly finished. I’m packaging the original renders, patch evidence, source hashes, and exact commands into `result.md`.

LeakSanitizer cannot finish in this execution environment; it reports a tracing limitation. I’m completing the address/undefined-behavior check with leak detection disabled and will record that limit. I also refined the private fix to reset the authored wave offsets before restart, preventing repeated visits from shifting the wave’s starting position.

Delivered [result.md](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/ui-render-check/result.md), [contact sheet](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/ui-render-check/renders/original/contact-sheet.png), and [exact commands](/mnt/d/WSL/esp32s31-delivery/factory-demo-port-e403/ui-render-check/commands.sh).

- Dashboard and all 12 coffee screens rendered with real LVGL at 800×480 RGB565.
- All 36 sampled coffee frames exactly match upstream.
- 25 transitions and 24 destruction cycles verified.
- Two animation-reentry defects confirmed; a verified private patch is included.
- ASan/UBSan found no errors; leak detection was unavailable.

Everything remains under the requested directory. No maintained-source edits or hardware claims.
